scope.time_horizon: Recorded acquisition times represented in seconds.

assertions.rationale: The dataset retains actual image–time pairs rather than replacing acquisition times with uniform indices. Recorded times enter conditioning and unequal-gap temporal regularization. Injection-relative versus precontrast-relative time origin remains ambiguous; subsecond precision is not established.

scope.time_horizon: Recorded acquisition times represented in seconds.

assertions.rationale: Actual examination acquisition times are retained as image–time pairs and encoded for prediction. They are distinguished from inserted virtual times. The reported median sequence interval is not substituted for each actual timestamp. Exact time-origin alignment and subsecond precision remain unresolved.

Acquisition time is described, but reconstruction completion or other information-release times are not distinguished from acquisition. The paper does not document availability-aware training-query construction.

The methods do not specify when reconstructed images or lesion-localization information become available to an intended noncontrast query. Acquisition timestamps alone do not establish information-availability semantics.

Observed acquisition times and generated intermediate times are distinguished in the LDL construction, but no measured/missing/invalid indicator supplied to the prediction model is reported. Sparse-time interpolation is not itself an availability mask.

The breast preprocessing and generator descriptions do not report missingness or image-validity masks consumed by the model. Lesion cropping and the observed-versus-virtual time construction do not establish this feature.

The baseline-to-query elapsed time is represented globally. No per-variable or per-measurement freshness representation, carry-forward policy, or freshness update mechanism is reported; the global time condition is insufficient for this criterion.

Requested elapsed time conditions generation from one baseline image, but measurement-specific age and updating under asynchronous observations are not described. Neither presence nor an incompatible carry-forward implementation is established.

scope.time_horizon: Irregular acquisition and requested prediction times in seconds.

assertions.rationale: Actual elapsed time conditions image generation through CLIP, while LDL explicitly uses unequal adjacent time gaps in its temporal penalty. This establishes an implemented irregular-time mechanism, not accuracy at every unobserved time, continuous-time physiological integration, or a validated effective horizon.

scope.time_horizon: Irregular acquisition and requested prediction times in seconds.

assertions.rationale: The breast configuration uses elapsed-time conditioning and the unequal-gap LDL operator with its separately reported training settings. No isolated test establishes the benefit or fidelity of this mechanism across irregular sampling regimes.

The paper describes manually controlled sparse acquisition and uses acquired times as conditions, but reports no conditional rule or model for when, whether or why an observation occurs. Time conditioning and synthetic densification alone do not satisfy the observation-process criterion.

Acquisition variability, scanner descriptions and the reported median intersequence interval characterize the data, but no observation-occurrence or informative-missingness model conditional on patient/acquisition context is reported.

Sparse sampling motivates the method, but no target-specific grid witness-preservation audit across values, update patterns, native timing and external acquisition channels is reported. LDL smoothness and generated renal curves are different assessments.

The breast experiments do not define and test an observation-clock witness distinction at a specified grid resolution. Adjacent-frame cSSIM and three-timepoint lesion examples do not establish such an audit.

Registration, resizing and normalization are reported, but source-specific measurement definitions and intensity units are not mapped through traceable conversions to a declared semantic/unit schema. Common tensor dimensions and an output normalization range alone do not establish this feature.

Multiple scanner manufacturers and field strengths are described, but no source-specific semantic or intensity-unit harmonization contract is reported. The relationship between normalized inputs and the intensity scale used for rMSE remains insufficiently specified.

Different training/test acquisition times are mentioned, but patient/slice partitioning, overlap checks, training-only preprocessing fits and validation-only hyperparameter selection are not reported. The description does not establish either leakage control or actual leakage.

Examination/patient/slice separation, repeated-examination overlap, lesion-location availability and training-only preprocessing/model selection are not audited in the reported protocol. A distinction between training and test times does not establish these controls.

No site-local data-retention arrangement, federated training/query procedure or exchanged-artifact protocol is reported. A private dataset and an A100 training-hardware description establish neither federation nor explicit identifiable-record central pooling.

Use of a public imaging resource is reported without a federated execution or data-access protocol. Public availability and scanner diversity do not establish federation, privacy guarantees or its explicit absence.

The baseline image is operationally encoded through the zero-convolution conditioning pathway, whose features enter latent-diffusion layers. CLIP encodes the time condition. Execution is supported by the implementation description and reported model experiments, but encoder-specific effectiveness is not separately tested.

The separately trained breast configuration uses the described image-condition encoder and CLIP time-conditioning pathway. An operational observation-to-feature mapping is established; this does not establish a persistent clinical belief state or encoder robustness.

assertions.value: No context-to-target representation-prediction objective in the reported MRI CEKWorld training stages.
assertions.rationale: The complete reported objectives are diffusion noise regression plus LAL template-distance regularization, followed by diffusion noise regression plus LDL temporal-difference regularization. The template aggregates generated latent statistics, and LDL penalizes derivatives; neither supplies a context-to-target representation prediction term. Latent diffusion and a VAE bottleneck do not themselves satisfy this predictive-latent feature. This assessment does not assert anything about unreported pretraining of inherited encoders.

assertions.value: No context-to-target representation-prediction objective in the reported MRI CEKWorld training stages.
assertions.rationale: The breast configuration changes regularization strength, not objective type. Its specified training uses noise prediction, generated-template alignment and latent temporal smoothing rather than prediction of a separately defined target representation from context. Absence is scoped to these fully described training objectives, not inferred merely from missing JEPA terminology.

assertions.applicability_reason: This feature concerns anti-collapse design for a context/target predictive-representation objective. The complete paper-described training stages instead use diffusion noise regression with template and smoothness penalties, without that representation-learning objective. This dependency-specific exclusion does not exclude generative mode collapse, excessive smoothing or dynamic suppression as relevant hazards.
assertions.rationale: Neither the VAE bottleneck nor covariance shrinkage is coded as a predictive-representation anti-collapse mechanism. Covariance shrinkage addresses numerical positive-definiteness.

assertions.applicability_reason: The breast configuration has no context/target predictive-representation training objective to which this feature's anti-collapse dependency applies. Its reported objectives are diffusion noise regression, template alignment and temporal smoothing. Generic generative collapse or loss of enhancement dynamics remains a separate applicable concern.
assertions.rationale: A specific dependency, rather than research status or lack of evaluation, justifies this narrow inapplicability judgment.

assertions.value: No direct reconstructed-observation-versus-observation loss in the reported MRI CEKWorld training objectives.
assertions.rationale: The specified objectives compare predicted noise with sampled noise and regularize generated latent statistics and temporal differences. They do not compare decoded reconstructed images or observed values against observations. Ground-truth image encoding, VAE decoding and evaluation-time image-fidelity metrics are not reconstruction-loss terms. This absence applies only to the paper-described training stages; inherited VAE pretraining is not established by this assessment.

assertions.value: No direct reconstructed-observation-versus-observation loss in the reported MRI CEKWorld training objectives.
assertions.rationale: The breast training stages use the same fully specified noise-prediction and latent-regularization objectives with a different spatial weight. No decoded-image reconstruction loss appears in those objectives. Reported PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS and rMSE are evaluation metrics, not evidence of such a training loss. No conclusion is transferred from the cited VAE's presumed pretraining.

The encoded baseline and learned time-conditioned diffusion advance the origin to observed later enhancement images, supporting L1 without requiring recurrence or cross-call filtering. No settable dose/action comparison supports L2/L3; no identified contrast-effect claim. Patient-disjoint split remains unresolved, so no R2 inferred.

The encoded baseline and learned time-conditioned diffusion advance the origin to observed later enhancement images, supporting L1 without requiring recurrence or cross-call filtering. No settable dose/action comparison supports L2/L3; no identified contrast-effect claim. Patient-disjoint split remains unresolved, so no R2 inferred.

scope.rationale: Existing actual clinical images are evaluated offline, but the stated test-set mention does not provide a sufficient split design to establish held-out retrospective internal validation. No alternative readiness facet is established. This is not an assertion that all facets are absent.

Human examination data and test results are reported, but unique-patient counts and examination/patient partitioning are not reported. Multiple scanners and a separate dataset-specific training configuration do not establish R3. No actual reader or prospective system-use study is reported.

gate_assessments.rationale: Dataset names, counts and preprocessing are described, but partitioning unit/counts, patient overlap, registration quality control, lesion-localization availability, and model-selection separation are insufficiently reported. A statement about different test times is not a leakage-control protocol.

Reported baseline-to-later-image prediction supports L1, but a carried evolving state is not established. Non-leaky reference evaluation is also unresolved. Direct time-conditioned generation must not be relabeled as recurrent learned world-state rollout.

scope.time_horizon: Multiple requested clinical times; selected breast images to 462 s.

gate_assessments.rationale: Multi-time generation is shown, but no horizon-resolved reference error, declared tolerance, effective horizon or drift test is reported. Generation at synthetic intermediate times and smoothness of generated curves do not establish accuracy there.

The evaluated use reports image fidelity and smoothness, not probabilistic coverage guarantees or uncertainty-dependent decisions. This gate is outside that limited claim. Predictive uncertainty and calibration remain not_reported rather than validated or intrinsically inapplicable.

The fully described inference function takes baseline MRI and requested time, not settable clinical or acquisition actions. Contrast administration is background to the acquired data, not an encoded alternative action.

No intervention-effect estimand or contrast-agent/dose alternative is evaluated. Claims of physiological fidelity are not identified causal effects. A causal gate would become applicable before interpreting new action-conditioned outputs as intervention effects.
The described system is a conditional image generator with no model-coupled optimizer or learned decision policy. Hyperparameter optimization and diffusion denoising are not clinical planning.

scope.population: Potential clinical contrast-replacement use claimed by the authors.

gate_assessments.rationale: If generated enhancement is used to replace acquired contrast imaging or inform diagnosis, incorrect pathology or kinetics could affect care. No evaluated clinical guard, abstention, escalation threshold or fallback is reported. This does not establish that the research implementation lacks every safeguard.

scope.population: Claimed generality across tissues and datasets.

gate_assessments.rationale: Two dataset-specific settings and selected organ examples are not independent frozen-model external validation. Site/time splits, adaptation rules, overlap controls, subgroup testing and external transport are not reported.

Actual clinical images are used, but no defined actual clinician/reader evaluation or matched simulation-to-physical utility study is reported. Author interpretation of montages is not a human evaluation study.

Risk avoidance, lower cost and downstream diagnostic use are claimed benefits. No prospective system-use protocol, patient/workflow utility endpoint, harms measurement or comparative clinical evaluation establishes these benefits.

No operational clinical deployment or release for an authorized clinical use is described. A future research code URL is not such a release. Operational governance would require a new intended-use assessment.

The source hash and local availability are inherited from the supplied record; neither was independently recomputed or checked.
Feature assertions are deliberately empty as requested. This package is not a completed 128-feature annotation or a completed semantic-validation pass.
Functional L1 future-image prediction does not by itself establish the persistent-state requirement for verified core-WM membership.

The complete inference formulation is baseline image plus requested time. No reusable clinical-state recurrence, measured re-assimilation, settable intervention input, alternative-action comparison, or planner is demonstrated.
Clinical time, diffusion denoising time, optimization epochs, and the two training stages are different coordinates.
Actual clinical imaging datasets are used, but split unit, allocation counts, patient/examination overlap controls and validation-set model selection are not reported. R2 remains unresolved.
The 922 breast examination records must not be equated with 922 unique patients; abdominal and breast counts must not be pooled as a single patient denominator.
Detailed eligibility, demographic distribution, diagnoses, acquisition-site count and subgroup evaluation are not reported.
Registered abdominal images may improve apparent anatomical alignment, but registration algorithm, residual error and quality control are not reported.
Lesion-centered breast cropping uses tumor locations; the availability and source of that localization at the intended noncontrast decision point are not evaluated.
Requested-time generalization is not shown to be patient-independent. The relationship between injection-time and precontrast-image-time origins is unclear.
Virtual intermediate-time predictions are synthetic regularization targets, not acquired dense human ground truth.
Table 1 has no test denominator, confidence intervals, repeated-run variability or statistical tests. Metric-specific time grids and aggregation units are not fully reported.
PSNR units are not explicitly labeled; rMSE evaluation scaling and its relationship to [−1,1] input normalization are insufficiently specified.
cSSIM measures adjacent-frame similarity rather than correct kinetic evolution; it can favor inadequate temporal change and does not normalize for unequal time gaps.
Figure 6 compares normalized generated renal curves without a measured ground-truth curve, numerical vertical scale, sample denominator or uncertainty.
Selected organ and breast montages lack case-selection rules, independent case counts, case-specific pathological confirmation, blinded reader assessment and diagnostic endpoints.
PCA clustering and smooth latent organization do not establish correct physiological dynamics, personalization, or state sufficiency.
Patient conditioning and a patient-specific training template are not proof of personalized predictive value; history/baseline-swap controls are not reported.

LAL uses channel covariance aggregated over spatial locations, which does not uniquely preserve spatial anatomy. Template provenance and mean-covariance versus transformed-vector averaging descriptions are ambiguous.
The purported equidistance objective minimizes squared distances to the template; it does not explicitly equalize distances. Claims about preserved dynamic diversity are not mathematical guarantees.

The supplementary second-difference derivation contains a sign inconsistency and an unrestricted second-order-accuracy claim needing spacing assumptions. The weighted operator is not the ordinary unweighted derivative stencil.
Early-time outlier explanations, Ki=0 versus Ki≥1, figure panel lettering, PCA time-color wording, and acquisition/visualization timestamps contain unresolved source inconsistencies.
The claim of leading all breast spatial metrics conflicts with the higher CCNet PSNR in Table 1. Ablation percentages and metric/module attribution are also unclear.
Comparator nonconvergence under shared hyperparameters limits claims of adequately tuned head-to-head superiority.
Diffusion stochasticity is not calibrated predictive uncertainty. No uncertainty decomposition, calibration study, trajectory coverage, or uncertainty-based decision rule is reported.
No quantitative error-versus-horizon criterion, tolerance-based effective horizon, or recursive drift evaluation is reported.
Anatomical invariance and smoothness are regularization priors, not identified pharmacokinetic mechanisms or causal intervention effects.
Contrast avoidance, lower costs, diagnostic reliability and clinical universality are author claims, not demonstrated patient/workflow benefits.
No actual expert reader study, prospective shadow use, prospective intervention, comparative effectiveness study, authorization, or operational monitoring is reported.

Safety guards, abstention, privacy controls, security testing, ethics approval and governance compliance are not sufficiently reported; research status does not establish their absence or inapplicability.
Code is announced in the paper. Current repository accessibility, implementation details, released weights and licensing were not checked.
References were read as bibliography entries; cited systems were not independently retrieved and their capabilities were not transferred to MRI CEKWorld.
No structural JSON Schema validator, cross-reference engine, graph assembly, regression test, or external code execution was run in this response.
